title: Human-Centric Lighting in Classroom Design: Effects on Student Cognition and Performance – A Systematic Review
review_question: To review research on the impact of Human-Centric Lighting (HCL) design, simulating natural light cycles, on student concentration, cognitive abilities, academic performance, and overall well-being in educational institutions.
inclusion_exclusion_criteria: Peer-reviewed empirical studies published within the last ten years, focusing on the interaction between lighting and education, selected based on relevance, timeliness, and source quality.

findings.antecedent: Human-Centric Lighting (HCL) systems simulating natural day and night cycles
findings.consequent: attention, working memory, information processing speed, executive functions, overall academic performance, concentration, academic efficiency, cognitive functions, learning
findings.quote: HCL systems... can improve attention, working memory, information processing speed, executive functions, and overall academic performance of students.

findings.antecedent: Lighting with high levels of blue light in the morning and warmer tones towards the evening
findings.consequent: synchronize circadian rhythms, students' cognitive functions, emotional states
findings.quote: Specifically, lighting that provides high levels of blue light in the morning and warmer tones towards the evening successfully helps synchronize circadian rhythms, directly improving students' cognitive functions and emotional states.

synthesis_conclusions: Human-Centric Lighting (HCL) positively impacts student academic performance and overall well-being.
HCL systems, by simulating natural light cycles, can improve cognitive functions (attention, memory, processing speed, executive functions) and reduce fatigue.

Specific light parameters, such as high levels of blue light in the morning and warmer tones towards the evening, are effective in synchronizing circadian rhythms and improving cognitive and emotional states.
HCL should be integrated into educational strategies and infrastructure to create optimal learning environments.
evidence_gaps: Lack of long-term studies exploring the lasting effects of HCL on academic performance and student health.
Most existing studies focus on short-term outcomes, leaving questions about long-term benefits and potential risks unanswered.
Methodological limitations in many studies, such as small sample sizes and lack of control groups, affecting generalizability.
Controversies and contradictory results regarding the optimal parameters of HCL.
Potential negative effects of excessive blue light exposure, particularly in the evening, which can disrupt natural circadian rhythms and sleep quality.
Need for more detailed research on how different intensities and spectra of light affect various age groups and types of students.
Future research should explore how individual differences among students impact the effectiveness of HCL.

limitations: Variability of study designs and sample sizes may affect the generalizability of the findings.
Lack of long-term studies limits the understanding of the enduring effects of HCL.
